title: Manager, Security and Information Assurance (Permanent)
description:
Header

Security & Information Assurance Manager (Permanent)

Halifax NS, Winnipeg MB, Ottawa ON, Victoria BC

Expected Salary $88,641 to $116,341

To determine final salary, Babcock considers a variety of factors including the successful Candidate’s skills and experience and internal equity. The final base salary offer is at the Company’s sole discretion and presented as part of a competitive total compensation package.

Your Role

What You Do Here Matters

In a complex world marked by the threat of war, natural disasters, and geopolitical instability, national security has never been more important.

Babcock is an international defence company providing support and product solutions to enhance our customers’ defence capabilities and critical assets.

Our Canadian team combines their talent and expertise with deep global knowledge and experience from our operations in the United Kingdom, Europe, Australasia and Africa.

Working for us, you’ll help ensure that Canada’s critical services and assets are readily available, reliable, and capable for our defence and civil customers and contribute to Babcock’s Purpose, ‘Creating a safe and secure world, together.’

Be Part of Something Big.

Babcock is a people business. Our people and customers matter most to us. Here you will experience a challenging and rewarding work environment with the support you need to deliver and thrive in your career alongside inclusive teams you respect that value your skills and dedication.

Our Babcock Principles create the foundation for how we deliver better outcomes for our Culture, Customers and Communities. By collectively embodying these Principles in all the work we do, our colleagues help make us great:

- Be Curious – We believe in challenging the status quo and asking, ‘how might we?’

- Think: Outcomes – We believe in measuring success by the results we deliver and the positive impact we make

- Be Kind – We believe in being kind to ourselves, kind to each other, and kind to our planet.

- Collaborate – We believe that Babcock is greater than the sum of its parts.

- Be Courageous – We believe in being brave, ambitious, and determined.

- Own and Deliver – We believe everybody has a part to play in Babcock’s and our customers’ success.

Our people are at the heart of creating a safe and secure world. We offer a collection of programs and benefits designed to support their well-being:

Health & Well-being

- 100% employer-paid health and dental premiums

- Our Wellness benefit promotes a work environment that supports healthy lifestyles and well-being

- Our Employee and Family Assistance Plan (EFAP) offers support and solutions for a wide range of life’s challenges

- A Maternity/Parental Leave top-up payment is available for our colleagues as their family grows

Planning for the Future

- Babcock Canada matches a portion of earnings towards our RRSP/DPSP program. Additionally, colleagues can contribute directly to a TFSA

Flexibility in How We Work

- We offer an agile workplace for several positions

- An option of a compressed work schedule supports work/life interests

- Competitive annual vacation time off and additional time off during our holiday closure

Growth and recognition

- A comprehensive colleague recognition program and bonus program

- Training and support for professional development and professional membership dues

We encourage you to learn more about Babcock Canada by exploring our website: babcockcanada.com.

Description

In this role, you will:

- Lead and administer Babcock Canada's Security and Information Assurance Program as Company Security Officer, ensuring compliance with contractual, regulatory, customer, and corporate requirements.

- Develop, implement, and continuously improve security objectives, policies, standards, procedures, metrics, and assurance activities that support business objectives and regulatory compliance.

- Act as the primary point of contact for customers, regulators, and government security authorities on security program matters.

- Interpret and implement security requirements arising from contracts, regulations, the Industrial Security Program, the Controlled Goods Program, and corporate policies.

- Assess security threats, vulnerabilities, and risks; recommend mitigation strategies; and provide expert security advice to leadership and business stakeholders.

- Lead security assurance activities, including audits, inspections, monitoring, investigations, reporting, and corrective actions, and assess the effectiveness of security controls and program performance.

- Collaborate with IT and cybersecurity teams to align physical, personnel, information, and cyber security controls and protect classified, protected, and sensitive information and assets.

- Oversee personnel security, facility security, access control, secure area accreditation, Controlled Goods Program activities, and related security administration requirements.

- Provide security oversight, due diligence, and advice for contracts, suppliers, projects, business pursuits, acquisitions, partnerships, and other organizational initiatives.

- Support travel security, incident response, emergency management, business continuity, crisis management, and organizational resilience activities as required.

- Promote a positive security culture through awareness, engagement, education, and training initiatives across the organization.

- Perform other duties as assigned.

The ideal canadidate brings:

- Minimum 8 years of experience in corporate, government, defence, industrial, or regulated security environments, including administration of the Industrial Security Program and Controlled Goods Program.

- Experience developing and implementing security policies, procedures, risk management, compliance, and assurance programs.

- Knowledge of physical and personnel security, including access control, investigations, audits, security clearances, screening, and visitor management.

- Understanding of information security, cybersecurity, business continuity, and emergency management principles.

- Strong analytical, problem-solving, report writing, communication, stakeholder engagement, and influencing skills, including the ability to communicate effectively with senior leaders, customers, regulators, and government agencies.

- Post-secondary education in Security Management or a related field is an asset.

- Project management experience or certification is an asset.

- Bilingualism (English/French) is an asset.

- Eligibility to obtain and maintain NATO Secret clearance, Controlled Goods registration, and ITAR eligibility.

One that welcomes everyone to contribute to our success regardless of race, national or ethnic origin, colour, religion, age, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, marital status, family status, genetic characteristics, or disability, and conviction for an offence for which a pardon has been granted or in respect of which a record suspension has been ordered. title: Security Graduate Programme
description:
Security Graduate Programme

Programme title: Security Graduate Programme

Salary: Minimum £35,000. Salary is dependent on location, role and qualifications.

Location: Rosyth, Fife, Scotland

Application closing date: 20 October 2026

Programme start date: September 2027

Role ID:

What will you do on the programme?

On the Security Graduate Programme, you’ll help keep our projects, people and information secure across marine and nuclear work at Rosyth, gaining practical experience in a highly regulated environment.

You’ll work with teams across the business to ensure the right security measures are in place from the start of each project and within supplier contracts. This includes identifying and managing risks, and working with customers to meet required standards.

You’ll also contribute to improving security policies and raising awareness across areas such as cyber, information protection and physical security, while building relationships across teams.

By supporting audits and working alongside experienced Security Managers, you’ll develop a strong understanding of how security operates in practice – equipping you with the skills and experience to build a career in this important and evolving field.

How is the programme structured?

This two-year graduate programme is based at Rosyth Royal Dockyard and is designed to give you broad experience across a range of projects.

Alongside developing your understanding of site security, you’ll work on a variety of on-site projects and contracts, including major shipbuilding programmes such as the Type 31 frigate programme, building a strong practical understanding of how security operates within a defence environment.

Rotations are flexible, with placement lengths varying depending on project needs. This means you may move between different areas throughout the programme, gaining exposure to a wide range of work and developing diverse skills.

As you progress, you’ll have the opportunity to shape your experience by aligning placements with your interests and career goals, helping you build expertise in the areas that matter most to you.

How do we develop and support you?

From day one, you’ll receive structured support, tailored training, and dedicated mentorship to help you excel throughout your programme and beyond.

You’ll join our Graduate Development Programme, featuring expert-led masterclasses on communication, personal branding, resilience, and wellbeing.

To support your professional development and broaden your knowledge, you’ll also be enrolled in a range of specialist courses, including the DISA Role of the Facility Security Controller, Introduction to Personal Security and Vetting, and IT and Cyber Security, as well as WINS Nuclear Security Fundamentals.

You’ll also be supported to gain membership with The Security Institute, with the opportunity to progress to Chartered status.

What’s waiting for you after the programme?

When you complete the programme, you’ll move into a permanent role within our Rosyth Security team, where you can build on what you’ve learned and continue to develop your expertise. You’ll also have ongoing support to progress towards professional chartership.

From there, your development doesn’t stop. We’ll support you as you grow into more senior roles and take on greater responsibility. Through the Babcock Role Framework, you’ll have a clear view of how your career can progress, with mapped-out pathways, development opportunities and the tools you need to get wherever you want to go.

What rewards and benefits will you get?

We want you to feel supported, valued and excited about what’s ahead. That’s why we offer a comprehensive package designed to support your development, your wellbeing and your life outside of work too.

In addition to a minimum starting salary of £35,000, you’ll benefit from:

- A minimum of 25 days of holiday plus bank holidays

- Generous pension and employee share schemes

- Flexible benefits, including cycle to work scheme, discounts

- Wellbeing support, covering mental, physical, financial, and social wellbeing, with services like our Employee Assistance Programme, digital GP service, and health checks.

You’ll also have the chance to get involved in our STEM outreach activities and volunteering opportunities.

What do you need to apply?

- You'll need to have achieved, or be on track to achieve, a degree in Security related subject, such as Cyber Security, Computer Science, Information Security, Digital Forensics, Software Engineering, Information Technology, Mathematics, Ethical Hacking or Network Security.

- Many of our programmes are subject to Security Clearance and Trade Control restrictions which mean that your place of birth, nationality, citizenship, or residency you hold or have held may impact which programmes you are eligible for. For this programme, you must be able to achieve and maintain Baseline Personnel Security Standard (BPSS) and Security Check (SC) clearance. For further details, visit GOV.UK and search ‘United Kingdom Security Vetting: clearance levels’.

- Under applicable national security legislation, this post may only be occupied by a sole UK national. This legal requirement is independent of our recruitment policies, and all eligible applicants will be assessed fairly and without discrimination.

Where will you be based?

Places on our Security Graduate Programme for September 2027 are available in our Marine sector in Rosyth.

Our 320-acre Rosyth facility is home to one of the largest and most modern waterside advanced manufacturing and repair facilities in the UK. At Rosyth, we specialise in the design, build and through-life support of complex naval and commercial marine assets.

We offer agile working, giving you some flexibility, but you can expect to spend several days a week on-site as part of your role and development. By your start date, you must be able to reliably commute to the site. This will normally require living within a reasonable commuting distance of Rosyth or relocating before you join us.

Once you’ve successfully completed the programme, you’ll continue your career in the same location, so it’s worth considering this when applying.

Application process and important information

Applications are reviewed in the order they are received, and if there’s a high level of interest in this programme, we may close applications earlier than advertised. To give yourself the best chance of being considered, we recommend submitting your application and completing any required online assessments as soon as possible.

Please apply to one programme only. If we receive more than one application from you, we’ll assess the first one submitted. If your chosen programme becomes oversubscribed, we may contact you to discuss other programmes you could be eligible for.

We're a Disability Confident Employer. If you require additional support or adjustments during the recruitment process, please let us know when you apply. Our team will contact you after receiving your application to discuss your requirements and the support available.

We’re committed to building an inclusive culture where everyone’s free to thrive. We are happy to talk about flexible working – please ask about alternative patterns of work at interview.
